findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "cortex_ask" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: The user's real, private memory — their email, calendar, files, contacts, and every fact agents have remembered — fused across vector, full-text and graph searc…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "cortex_ask" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: The user's real, private memory — their email, calendar, files, contacts, and every fact agents have remembered — fused across vector, full-text and graph searc…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: cortex_ask, search_docs · Private data: cortex_ask · Public sink: cortex_ask, cortex_manifest.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: cortex_ask, search_docs · Private data: cortex_ask · Public sink: cortex_ask, cortex_manifest

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
